title: Engineering programs in Europe that accept the Duolingo English Test
summary: Explore engineering programs across Europe that accept the Duolingo English Test, from chemical engineering and computing to materials and sustainable technology.
body_markdown:
Many engineering programs in Europe accept the[Duolingo English Test](https://bit.ly/3Dn1elO?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) (DET) as proof of English proficiency for international applicants. Students can use the DET when applying to engineering programs at institutions including Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, the University of Limerick, Montanuniversität Leoben, the University of Chemistry and Technology Prague, and Constructor University, with additional options across Belgium, the Czech Republic, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Spain, and Austria.


These universities offer opportunities to study fields ranging from civil and chemical engineering to materials science, computing, energy, and sustainable technologies. For international students exploring where to study engineering in Europe, that means plenty of options for finding a program that fits both their academic interests and preferred destination.


## Europe offers engineering programs across a wide range of specializations


Europe is home to comprehensive research universities, specialized engineering schools, and technology-focused institutions. Together, they give students opportunities to pursue mechanical, civil, chemical, electrical, materials, computer, and other engineering disciplines.


Your interests can help narrow the search. Students interested in materials and natural resources might explore Austria’s Montanuniversität Leoben, while future chemical engineers can consider specialized institutions such as CPE Lyon or the University of Chemistry and Technology Prague. Students interested in civil engineering, architecture, computing, and sustainable technologies can find options across the continent.


Ireland offers another strong option for international engineering students, with broad engineering programs at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, and the University of Limerick.


## These engineering programs in Europe accept the Duolingo English Test


International students can use the DET to meet English proficiency requirements at engineering programs across Europe, including programs in Austria, Belgium, the Czech Republic, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, and Spain.


- [Trinity College Dublin](https://www.tcd.ie/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in Ireland accepts the DET and offers engineering specialisms including biomedical; civil, structural and environmental; computer; electronic; and mechanical and manufacturing engineering.
- [University College Dublin](https://www.ucd.ie/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in Ireland accepts the DET and offers pathways in biomedical, chemical and bioprocess, civil, electrical and electronic, mechanical, and sustainable systems engineering, as well as structural engineering with architecture.
- [University of Limerick](https://www.ul.ie/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in Ireland accepts the DET and gives international students another option for pursuing engineering in an English-speaking European university environment.
- [Montanuniversität Leoben](https://www.unileoben.ac.at/en/technical-university-of-leoben/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in Austria accepts the DET and offers specialized engineering programs in areas including circular engineering, geoenergy, energy, materials science, mechanical engineering, mineral resources, metallurgy and recycling, and environmental technology.
- [University of Chemistry and Technology Prague](https://www.vscht.cz/?jazyk=en&ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in the Czech Republic accepts the DET and offers English-taught study in areas including chemical engineering, materials, chemical engineering and bioengineering, hydrogen engineering, and environmental technology.
- [Brno University of Technology](https://www.vut.cz/en/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) ’s[Faculty of Civil Engineering](https://www.czechuniversities.com/catalogue-of-universities/faculty-of-civil-engineering?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in the Czech Republic accepts the DET, giving international students an option specifically focused on civil engineering.
- [Constructor University](https://constructor.university/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in Bremen, Germany accepts the DET and offers programs including Electrical and Computer Engineering, Robotics and Intelligent Systems, and Industrial Engineering & Management.
- [IQS](https://iqs.edu/en/?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) at[Ramon Llull University](https://www.url.edu/en?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) in Spain accepts the DET and offers engineering degrees including Chemical Engineering and Industrial Engineering.


These are some of the engineering programs in Europe that accept the Duolingo English Test. English proficiency requirements can vary by degree and program, so international applicants should check the current requirements for the specific program they plan to apply to.


## Your engineering interests can help you choose where to study in Europe


The right engineering program starts with the kind of problems you want to solve.


Students interested in chemical engineering can explore institutions with specialized expertise in Prague, Lyon, and Barcelona. Those interested in civil engineering and the built environment can investigate programs in Brno and Parma. Future engineers interested in materials, energy, and sustainability can look for programs that concentrate their teaching and research in those areas.


You can also consider the type of university experience you want. A comprehensive research university can give you access to disciplines beyond engineering, while a specialized institution can offer an academic environment concentrated around science and technology. Location, research opportunities, industry connections, course structure, and career goals can all help you refine your shortlist.


## The DET can help you take the next step toward studying engineering in Europe


Once you have found engineering programs that match your goals,[the DET](https://bit.ly/3Dn1elO?ref=blog.englishtest.duolingo.com) offers an accessible way to demonstrate your English proficiency. The test costs **$70 USD** , you can take it online from home, and certified results are typically available within 48 hours.


Start with the engineering discipline you want to pursue, compare programs and destinations, and check each program’s current English proficiency requirements. Your shortlist might take you from chemical engineering in Prague to sustainable technology in Austria or engineering and computing in Germany.
